mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES mobility after a sharp weekly drop predicts higher retail visits within four weeks because commuting restores weekday foot traffic near shopping corridors. If WORKPLACES stabilizes or rises from the current trough, RETAIL_REC should follow upward with a short lag.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -17.7 at t-1w to -29.9 at t-0w while TRANSIT fell from -47.0 to -59.7
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains at or below the current level for four weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises versus the prior four-week average, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility jumps above its recent range, people substitute away from discretionary outings and retail trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next one to two weeks. The effect should be strongest when the residential increase coincides with weaker WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above +10 points for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is +12.1 at t-0w after +5.9 to +8.1 in prior weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL exceeds +10 but RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next two weeks, or if retail rises despite continued high residential time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous downturn in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates tighter activity suppression, which should reduce retail-and-recreation mobility over the following four weeks. Retail is expected to lag the restriction signal because fewer commuters and fewer onsite workers reduce incidental shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -55 and WORKPLACES falls below -25 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -59.7 and WORKPLACES is -29.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below the trigger but RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the prior 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A broad decline in PARKS mobility after a warm-weather or outdoor-leisure peak signals weaker weekend movement overall, which should spill into lower retail-and-recreation visits within one week. The effect is strongest when the park drop is not offset by gains in grocery or residential movement.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by 10 points or more week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -20.0 to -27.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS drops by at least 10 points but RETAIL_REC does not fall within one week, the seasonal spillover claim is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed rise in GROCERY_PHARM alongside higher RESIDENTIAL mobility captures precautionary, stay-near-home behavior that crowds out discretionary shopping trips. Under this pattern, RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next two weeks as essential trips replace leisure retail outings.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell to -10.1 while RESIDENTIAL rose to +12.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both remain elevated but RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived shock where TRANSIT plunges below its recent average signals immediate avoidance of shared mobility, which suppresses retail-and-recreation visits within one week. If the transit shock reverses quickly, the retail decline should also be temporary.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -47.0 at t-1w to -59.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls by more than 8 points and RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week, the avoidance signal is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stay deeply negative for several weeks, a persistent restriction regime is already in place and retail mobility continues to drift downward over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if workplace mobility recovers without any retail rebound, because then retail is no longer tied to the restriction intensity.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has stayed below -17 and TRANSIT below -47 in all four weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain deeply negative but RETAIL_REC becomes less negative or positive over the next 28 days, the restriction persistence hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM indicates weekend and neighborhood circulation is recovering from the winter dip, which should lift retail-and-recreation mobility after about four weeks. The signal should only work once outdoor activity is no longer falling sharply.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by 5 points or more for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -27.4 at t-0w after being -27.4 and -20.0 in the prior two weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS does not recover for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next month, the seasonal recovery mechanism is rejected.
